$comment: Release manifest for candidate-2 (06-13-PLAN.md Task 2, 06-CONTEXT.md D-12/D-13).
Every value here is copied from a real continuous-integration run at the revision below.
Nothing in this file is measured locally. Where a lane has only local evidence, it is
recorded as BLOCKED with its reason, never as PASSED, because NOTHING LOCAL MAY BIND TO
LOCALLY BUILT BYTES (tooling/release-lanes.json).
WHAT CHANGED SINCE CANDIDATE-1, which is bound to revision 26628e1:
* The whole desktop workflow is green for the first time -- all six jobs succeeded.
* The macOS application is signed, notarized and stapled BY CONTINUOUS INTEGRATION.
* desktop-promote RAN and PASSED, so QUAL-03's clause 2 has a passing lane at last.
* A SLSA Build Level 2 provenance attestation exists and verifies.
* Both CycloneDX bills of materials exist and are retained under evidence/sbom/.
* 14 of 39 lanes PASS, against 11 of 39 at candidate-1.
WHAT DID NOT CHANGE: the repository-integrity workflow still FAILS. Four lanes are
BLOCKED on real, named, unfixed causes -- a HIGH-severity dependency advisory, a privacy
scan finding, and a non-idempotent toolchain step. They are not papered over here, and
candidate-1 is not retroactively improved by any of the above: its bytes are still
unsigned and unattested, and its own manifest still says so.
This manifest is EXPECTED to verify non-zero. 25 lanes are BLOCKED and each says why.
A non-zero verdict carrying stated reasons is the honest outcome at this revision; a pass
would require a release claim this revision's evidence does not support.
Verify with:  node tooling/verify-release.mjs --manifest .planning/releases/candidate-2/release-manifest.json
Offline with: the same command plus --offline (degrades only the attestation step).
READ THE ATTESTATION LINE CAREFULLY. verify-release.mjs reports attestation=UNVERIFIED for
every artefact entry here, online and offline. That is NOT a statement that no attestation
exists -- one does, it verifies, and its decoded statement is retained under
evidence/attestation/. It is a statement that the committed entries are RECORDS of the
released bytes rather than the bytes, and the attestation is over the bytes. Closing that
gap is .planning/WINDOWS.md row 96.

revision.runIdNote: Two workflows produce evidence at this revision. `runId` names desktop.yml's run for schema compatibility; `runIds` names both, and every lane entry's evidence file records which job it came from. desktop.yml SUCCEEDED at this revision; repository-integrity.yml FAILED, and the four lanes responsible each carry their own BLOCKED entry.
revision.visibilityNote: The repository was made public between candidate-1 and this revision. That is what unblocked attestations: GitHub refuses to persist an Actions attestation for a user-owned private repository. It also enabled private vulnerability reporting and branch protection on main (force-push and deletion denied, enforce_admins true). Visibility is recorded here because it is a precondition of this candidate's provenance claim, not an incidental fact.

artifacts.name: desktop-macos-app
artifacts.digestSha256Note: digestSha256 is the digest verify-release.mjs recomputes from the bytes at artifactPath, which are the package-manifest.json that CI job desktop-package emitted and uploaded, committed here verbatim. The application's own digest is applicationDigestSha256 below. The 129 MB application bytes are NOT committed to this repository; the committed bytes are the CI-produced record OF those bytes.

signing.statement: THESE CI-BUILT BYTES ARE SIGNED, NOTARIZED AND STAPLED, and this is the first candidate for which that is true. The desktop-package job imported the Developer ID identity into an ephemeral keychain (`1 identity imported.`), resolved it (`Desktop package signing: Developer ID identity resolved`) and completed notarization and stapling (`The staple and validate action worked!`). The committed package manifest records codeSigning.developerIdSigned=true, codeSigning.hardenedRuntime=true and notarization {attempted:true, status:"Accepted", stapled:true}. Verified out of band against the downloaded artefact: `spctl --assess` returns accepted with source=Notarized Developer ID. The signing identity's certificate subject and team identifier are deliberately NOT recorded anywhere in this repository; they carry personal data and this repository is public. WHAT THIS DOES NOT PROVE: that the bytes that were signed came from this repository -- that is the provenance attestation's job, recorded separately below -- or anything whatsoever about what is inside them. See docs/security/SUPPLY-CHAIN.md section 1.

attestation.verifiedNote: Verified out of band against the artefact downloaded from run 34735177060, which re-hashes to the attested subject digest byte for byte. verify-release.mjs's own attestation step CANNOT reproduce this: it is handed artifactPath, which is the committed record, not the attested bytes. It therefore prints attestation=UNVERIFIED here and that line must not be read as 'no attestation exists'. .planning/WINDOWS.md row 96.

lanes.reason: Physical blocker, and at this revision the row was not attempted at all. Row A14 changes the system appearance WHILE the app is running and asserts the window re-themes without a relaunch; that requires a logged-in Aqua session whose appearance daemon posts AppleInterfaceThemeChangedNotification, which a hosted GitHub runner has none of. Between candidate-1 and this revision the row was split out of the desktop-macos-integration job into this local-attested lane, so the job reports `rows=3` and no longer produces an A14 result either way. THE SPLIT DID NOT CLOSE THE ROW, it only stopped a physically impossible row from failing a job: the row is exactly as unrunnable in continuous integration as it was, and it reports BLOCKED with a zero case count here rather than disappearing. A local pass exists and is NOT recorded as a passing status, because it binds to locally built bytes. See .planning/WINDOWS.md row 84.

The lane may not report PASSED while unwired. TO CLOSE: pick option (a) or (b) in row 82. Owner: BACKLOG.
